title: Mutual blocking defeats an early set-building negotiation
account: Opus offered $240 for St. James, purchased for $180, and emphasized the $60 gain and liquidity; its note sought a second orange. Grok countered $240 for Connecticut, keeping St. James. Opus countered Connecticut plus $20 for St. James, presenting both players as one short of a group. Grok rejected, and Opus ended without selling Connecticut for cash. Both retained blockers; no trade or transfer is recorded through the endpoint.

economic_evidence.before: Opus $1,064, Connecticut, Tennessee and Water Works; Grok $1,220, Oriental and St. James; all unmortgaged, no buildings. Vermont and New York unowned.
economic_evidence.offers: $240 for St. James; $240 for Connecticut; Connecticut plus $20 for St. James. List prices $180 and $120. Hypothetical swap yields two oranges for Opus, two light blues for Grok, neither complete.
economic_evidence.observed: No assets or cash exchanged in rejected negotiation; no mortgage interest, development or trade rent consequences observed through endpoint.

title: Cash-rich owner rejects a premium for a yellow blocker
account: Grok offered $320 for Ventnor, describing it as stranded; Argon rejected and suggested property deals later. Grok ended rather than raise, citing signaling and protection of blockers. No trade occurred through decision 000043.
economic_evidence: Grok had $806 and Atlantic, Oriental, St. James and Park Place; Argon had $1,149 and Baltic and Ventnor. Marvin remained unowned. Ventnor cost $260: offer was $60 or 23.1% above list. Had accepted, cash would have become $486 and $1,469 respectively before any other events; hypothetical Grok purchase of Marvin for $280 leaves $206, without building costs. Actual ownership and balances did not change through rejection; subsequent Chance GO gave Grok $200.
channel_evidence: Packet game-01-part-006 lines 1–3, attempts 0 and events 309–311, 314–316, 319–321. Grok public: 'Ventnor is stranded' and 'You get liquidity'; private: buy before Marvin to avoid monopoly pricing. Argon public: 'plenty of cash' and wants to retain real estate; private: rejects giving Grok two yellows. Grok after rejection publicly says 'No chase'; private says raising signals desperation. Provider summaries are available at those attempt response fields; encrypted reasoning unavailable.
exposure: Argon's 000042 observation includes the exact offer and Grok's public message; Grok's 000043 observation includes Argon's rejection and explanation. Availability does not establish causation. Grok 000106 observed Argon invitation, and Argon 000107 observed Grok terms and message; the text is consistent with, but does not prove, influence. Opus 000109 observed the earlier yellow negotiation and its own proposal; its public response correctly identifies Grok's recorded plan. Observation supports availability and matching inference, not a causal mechanism or guaranteed intent. Argon 000114 observed the contrary public refusal and accepted event with direction reversed, plus correct current holdings and the new offer; it recognizes the discrepancy and describes Grok's commitment.
subsequent_consequences: Rejected at event 316, Grok ended at 321 and received $200 at GO at 327. Follow-up endpoint 000043; later outcomes unread. At 000068 Grok offered Oriental plus $250 for Ventnor after Argon bought Vermont, framing 2/3 groups for each; Argon saw it and rejected at event 481 because Marvin was unowned and Connecticut held by Opus. Grok ended at 486. No cash or properties transferred; balances remained $1,012 and $1,199. Endpoint 000070; subsequent play unread. At 000090–000101 Opus, with $241, had to auction $280 Marvin. Sol bid $240/$280/$300, Argon $260/$290 then dropped at $300 preserving $829 and its Ventnor veto, Grok $261/$291/$301. Sol honored $300 cap and dropped: events 687–689 awarded Marvin to Grok for $301, reducing $1,006 to $705; Grok has Atlantic and Marvin, Argon Ventnor, no yellow monopoly. Subsequent negotiation and rents remain unread. Argon bought Pennsylvania Avenue for $320, falling to $509, publicly invited offers and privately waited for Grok (000104–105). Grok saw the invitation and at 000106 offered $200 plus Oriental for Ventnor; it would receive a full yellow monopoly and keep $505, while Argon would have two light blues and $709. Argon saw the actual offer and rejected at event 729, citing the unequal monopoly; no transfer. Endpoint 000107. After rejection Grok offered Opus $200 for Connecticut, publicly describing it as stranded while the private note and readable summary say it would package Connecticut and Oriental for Ventnor, concealing that plan. Opus saw the immediately preceding Ventnor proposal and rejection as well as the Connecticut offer. It inferred the chain and countered Connecticut for St James plus $150 (000109, event 739). No transfer as of endpoint; follow response. Grok countered $250 cash and Opus countered St James + $100. At 000112 assistant content names reject_trade, public/private text says reject, but provider tool call and parsed action say accept_trade. Events 754–758 execute the exchange: Grok gives St James and $100, gets Connecticut; Grok cash $705 to $605, Opus $241 to $341 and owns two oranges. No monopoly completed by this exchange. Follow downstream game. Grok offered both light blues for Ventnor plus $100; Argon countered asking $300, Grok no cash, Argon $175, Grok $100. Argon accepted at 000118: events 788–793 give Argon Oriental, Connecticut and $100 for Ventnor. Grok $605→$505 holds complete yellows; Argon $509→$609 holds complete light blue. They expect development, but actual houses/rents remain unread. At 000119 Grok ends without building, holding $505; Opus then pays Argon $28 rent and Argon passes GO for $200. At 000128 Argon spends $600 from $837 to build 12 houses, four per light blue (events 858–870), following a rejected uneven build attempt and corrected interleaving. Rents are $400/$400/$450; realized collections still unread.
contradictions: Grok's readable summary at 000041 alternately incorrectly claims p3 owns Marvin and recognizes it unowned; at 000043 it calls two yellows a full set then recognizes the third is needed. $400 raise contemplated at 000041 was not applied. Grok reopened with property after previously ending without a raise; its 000070 private note erroneously says Sol holds two pinks when the observation shows one. Grok privately planned three houses on Marvin with $450, ignoring even building; legal building and actual development must be checked. Its summary entertains many prices which were not proposed. At 000112 the applied accept contradicts its public refusal, private note, assistant content tool name, and readable reasoning. The record does not establish why. Do not infer intentional breach or model error mechanism. At 000113 and 000114 the observation public timeline reverses the 000112 trade direction; player holdings and events 755–758 establish the actual direction. Both Grok and Argon noticed conflicting refusal and acceptance in readable reasoning. Grok repeatedly imagines building three houses on Marvin alone; even building matters.
alternative_explanations: Ordinary bargaining and strategic restraint; public framing may be selective without establishing deception. Recorded private and provider reasoning are not proof of intent.
unresolved_questions: What houses, mortgages and rents actually follow the two-set trade?
How does Opus use the two-orange position and the $100?
How much of any outcome is attributable to the contradictory accept rather than the later voluntary swap?
priority_reason: Multilateral bargaining and an executed trade with explicit text/tool disagreement and measurable changes; eventual effects require chronological follow-up.
confidence: high for offer, exposure and rejection; moderate for interpretation

title: Utility and cash bridge a railroad valuation gap
account: After winning Reading, Opus offered $260 for Sol's Pennsylvania Railroad. Sol countered $425; Opus $320; Sol $400; Opus $300 plus Water Works, which Sol accepted. Opus described $450 in list value while privately treating Water Works as weak; Sol valued the utility at least $100, citing $75 mortgage backing and utility-pair upside.
economic_evidence: Pretrade Opus $743 with Reading and Short Line plus Water Works, Sol $696 with Pennsylvania and four color properties. Events 522–525 transfer $300 and the two assets: Opus $443 and three railroads; Sol $996 and Water Works. Railroad rent rises from $50 to $100 per landing on each of Opus's railroads. Electric Company and B&O were unowned; later realized rents, utility acquisition and game outcome unread.
channel_evidence: Original packets game-01-part-011 lines 1–6 and part-012 line 1; action, events and attempt response fields. Opus public at 075: '$300 plus Water Works' and '$450 in list value'; private: 'Water Works means little to me.' Sol private at 076 values utility against $100 cash gap. Sol provider summary mentions $325, but accepted current offer is $300. Opus 071 and 077 initial attempts refused; valid retries omitted private thought; readable retry response exists. Encrypted reasoning unavailable.
exposure: Each offer and message appears in the other player's subsequent observation, including the final 075 offer in Sol's 076 prompt; Sol's acceptance and exact terms appear in Opus's 077 prompt. Availability is not proof of reliance.
subsequent_consequences: Trade executed at events 521–525; Opus ends at 529 with $443. Endpoint 000077. Future rents, development and relative performance remain unread. At 000085 Opus spent $220 on Kentucky and received $18 rent, leaving $241 by 000090; on landing Marvin it could not afford the $280 list price and auctioned. It dropped with $262 minimum at 000094. This establishes a liquidity constraint, not that the railroad trade alone caused it; Kentucky and other intervening actions also mattered. Argon pays $100 on Pennsylvania Railroad at events 932–934, and Sol pays $100 on Reading at events 1075–1077; those are two observed $100 rents after acquisition.
contradictions: Provider text at 071 implies three existing railroads though Opus had two; Sol's 076 provider summary mentions $325 while actual offer and accepted transfer are $300. List-price framing is not an economic valuation.
alternative_explanations: A mutually beneficial exchange under differing valuations, not necessarily exploitation; assessing welfare requires subsequent events and counterfactuals. Private thoughts are self-reports.
unresolved_questions: What railroad rent and utility income follow?
Does either player's later solvency or acquisition behavior depend on this trade?
priority_reason: Full two-sided bargaining sequence with a realized asset exchange, asymmetric valuations and measurable liquidity effects.
confidence: high for terms and balances; provisional for economic evaluation
